lines.content: BrotherGym is a **desktop application for gym trainers to manage the workout plans of their students, optimized for use through a Command Line Interface (CLI)** while retaining the benefits of a Graphical User Interface (GUI).
If you type quickly, BrotherGym can help you manage students and workouts faster than traditional GUI applications.
1. Ensure that Java `25` or later is installed on your computer.
**Mac users:** Ensure you have the precise JDK version prescribed [here](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html).
1. Copy the file to the folder you want to use as the _home folder_ for your BrotherGym.
1. Open a terminal, `cd` to the folder containing the JAR file, and run `java -jar brothergym.jar`.
A GUI similar to the one below should appear in a few seconds. Note how the app contains some sample data.
1. Type a command in the command box and press Enter to execute it. For example, type **`help`** and press Enter to open the help window.
Some example commands you can try:
* `addStudent John Doe --hp 98765432 --email johnd@example.com --addr John street, block 123, #01-01`:
Adds a student named `John Doe` to the BrotherGym student list.
* `viewStudent 2` : Selects the second student in the list to view all workout plans of that student.
Adds a plan named `Leg Day` to the workout plan list for the selected student.
* `viewPlan 2`: Selects the second plan of the selected student, to view all the exercises contained in that workout plan
* `addExercise Squats --description 30kg * 5 reps`: Adds an exercise called `Squats` in the selected workout plan.
* `deleteStudent 3` : Deletes the 3rd student shown in the current BrotherGym student list.
1. Refer to the [Features](#features) section below for details of each command.
* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `addStudent NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `--name NAME [--tag TAG]` can be used as `--name John Doe --tag friend` or as `--name John Doe`.
* Items followed by `...` can appear zero or more times.
For example, `[--tag TAG]... ` may be omitted, or written as `--tag friend` or `--tag friend --tag family`.
* Every `--tag` prefix must be followed by a non-empty alphanumeric tag. The valueless `--clearTags` flag is only
available for edit commands and must not be followed by a value.
* Parameters can be in any order.
For example, if the command specifies `--name NAME --hp PHONE_NUMBER`, `--hp PHONE_NUMBER --name NAME` is also acceptable.
* The format of commands should be abided by strictly. Additional parameters or prefixes would cause the command to not be processed.

* If you are using a PDF version of this document, be careful when copying and pasting commands that span multiple lines as space characters surrounding line-breaks may be omitted when copied over to the application.
Shows a message explaining how to access the help page.
Clears all entries from the BrotherGym student list.
Shows a list of all students in the BrotherGym student list and removes the selection from the selected student.
Adds a student to the BrotherGym student list.
Format: `addStudent NAME --hp PHONE_NUMBER --email EMAIL --addr ADDRESS [--tag TAG]... `
* Displays the updated BrotherGym student list after the new student is added.
* Name can only contain alphanumeric characters
* Phone number should be at least 3 digits long
* Email has to follow the format of `<name>@<domain>`
* Tag should not be multiple words long
**Tip:** A student can have any number of tags, including zero.
* `addStudent John Doe --hp 98765432 --email johnd@example.com --addr John street, block 123, #01-01`
* `addStudent Betsy Crowe --tag friend --email betsycrowe@example.com --addr Newgate Prison --hp 1234567 --tag criminal`
Edits an existing student in the BrotherGym student list.
Format: `editStudent STUDENT_ID [--name NAME] [--hp PHONE] [--email EMAIL] [--addr ADDRESS] [--tag TAG]... [--clearTags]`
* Edits the student at the specified `STUDENT_ID`. The student id refers to the index number shown in the displayed student list. The index **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
* At least one of the optional fields must be provided.
* Existing values will be updated to the input values.
* When editing tags, all of the student's existing tags are removed; adding tags is not cumulative.
* To remove all of a student's tags, enter `--clearTags` without a value.
* If both `--tag TAG` and `--clearTags` are supplied, all tags are cleared after the tag values are validated.
*  `editStudent 1 --hp 91234567 --email johndoe@example.com` Edits the phone number and email address of the 1st student to be `91234567` and `johndoe@example.com` respectively.
*  `editStudent 2 --name Betsy Crower --clearTags` Edits the name of the 2nd student to be `Betsy Crower` and clears all existing tags.
Finds students whose names contain any of the given keywords.
* The search is case-insensitive; for example, `hans` matches `Hans`.
* Keyword order does not matter; for example, `Hans Bo` matches `Bo Hans`.
* Only full words match; for example, `Han` does not match `Hans`.
* Students matching at least one keyword are returned (an `OR` search); for example, `Hans Bo` returns `Hans Gruber` and `Bo Yang`.
* At least one keyword must contain only letters and digits, following the student-name format.
Searches such as `find !!!` or `find Alice! Bob?` show an error and command usage.
Mixed input such as `find Alice !!!` still searches for `Alice`.
#### Viewing all workout plans of a student: `viewStudent`
Displays all the workout plans saved for the specified student.
* Displays the list of workout plans for the student at the specified `INDEX`,
which can now be edited through [workout plan commands](#workout-plan-related-commands)
* The student id refers to the index number shown in the displayed student list.
* The student id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
Deletes the specified student from the BrotherGym student list.
* Deletes the student at the specified `STUDENT_ID`.
* The student id refers to the index number shown in the displayed student list.
* The student id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
* `home` followed by `deleteStudent 2` deletes the 2nd student in the BrotherGym student list.
* `find Betsy` followed by `deleteStudent 1` deletes the 1st student in the results of the `find` command.
These commands can only be performed after a specific student has been selected via `viewStudent`
#### Add a workout plan to a student: `addPlan`
Add a new workout plan to the list of workout plans of the specified student
* Displays the updated list of workout plans of the specified student, after the new plan is added
* Name and description of the workout plan cannot be empty.
* Date field must be provided in `DDMMYYYY` format
#### Edit a workout plan of a student: `editPlan`
Edits an existing workout plan from the student's list of workout plans
Format: `editPlan PLAN_ID [--name PLAN_NAME] [--description DESCRIPTION] [--date DDMMYYYY] [--tag TAG]... [--clearTags]`
Dates follow the same calendar validation as `addPlan`, including leap-year checks.
* Edits the plan at the specified `PLAN_ID`.
The plan id refers to the index number shown in the displayed list of workout plans.
The plan id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
* At least one of the optional fields must be provided.
* Existing values will be updated to the input values.
* A new description cannot exceed 500 characters.
* When editing tags, all of the workout plan's existing tags are removed; adding tags is not cumulative.
* To remove all of a workout plan's tags, enter `--clearTags` without a value.
* If both `--tag TAG` and `--clearTags` are supplied, all tags are cleared after the tag values are validated.
Edits the description and date of the second workout plan of the student's list of workout plans
* `editPlan 3 --clearTags`: Clears all tags for the third workout plan of the student's list of workout plans
By default, workout plans have a `PENDING` status, which will change to `OVERDUE` when the `workoutDate` has passed.
* The status remains at `PENDING` when the current date is equal to the `workoutDate`,
only changing to `OVERDUE` on the next day
`markPlan` updates the status of a workout plan to `COMPLETED`.
* Marks the workout plan at the specified `PLAN_ID` as `COMPLETED`
* Shows an error if the workout plan is already marked as completed
* The plan id refers to the index number shown in the displayed list of workout plans
* The plan id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
`unmarkPlan` reverts the status of the workout plan to either `PENDING` or `OVERDUE`
* Reverts the status of the workout plan at the specified `PLAN_ID`
* Shows an error if the workout plan is already unmarked (`PENDING` or `OVERDUE`)
* The plan id refers to the index number shown in the displayed list of workout plans
* The plan id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
#### Viewing details of a workout plan: `viewPlan`
Expands the selected workout plan and its exercises within the current student's workout list.
* Keeps all of the student's workout plans visible in their original order and expands the selected plan in place.
* Displays the selected plan's title, date, status, description, tags, and numbered exercises. An empty plan shows `Exercises (0)` and an empty message.
* The plan id refers to the index number shown in the displayed list of workout plans of the student.
* The plan id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
* Run `viewPlan` again to expand a different plan, or `viewStudent` to collapse the selected plan. Exercise IDs follow the order displayed inside the expanded plan.
* The workout panel remains one scrollable list, so plans above and below the expanded plan remain accessible.
Example: `viewStudent 1` followed by `viewPlan 2` expands the second plan in place while retaining the surrounding workout cards.
![Example selected workout plan with sample exercises](images/selectedPlanView.png)
Deletes the specified workout plan from the list of workouts of the selected student.
* Deletes the workout plan at the specified `PLAN_ID`.
* The plan id refers to the index number shown in the displayed list of workout plans of the student.
* The plan id **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
Workout plans set the focus of a training session. Exercises specify the movements to perform during that session.
Select a student with `viewStudent`, then select one of their workout plans with `viewPlan` before adding an exercise.
#### Add an exercise to a workout plan: `addExercise`
* Both name and description are required and cannot be blank. The description can contain up to 500 characters.
* The exercise is appended to the selected workout plan. An identical name and description cannot be added twice.
* A workout plan can contain up to 100 exercises.
Edits one exercise in the selected workout plan.
* First select a student with `viewStudent STUDENT_ID`, then a workout plan with `viewPlan PLAN_ID`.
* `EXERCISE_ID` is the positive number shown beside the exercise in the selected plan view.
* Supply at least one field. An omitted field keeps its existing value and the exercise stays in the same position.
* Repeated or unsupported fields, invalid values, and edits that duplicate an existing exercise are rejected without changing the plan.
Example: `editExercise 2 --name Goblet Squat --description 3 sets of 10 reps`
Deletes one exercise from the selected workout plan.
* First select a student with `viewStudent STUDENT_ID`, then a plan with `viewPlan PLAN_ID`.
* `EXERCISE_ID` is the positive number shown beside the exercise in the selected plan.
* An invalid or out-of-range ID leaves the plan unchanged. The remaining exercises keep their order and are renumbered.
Example: `deleteExercise 2` removes the second exercise from the selected plan.
BrotherGym automatically saves data after every command. You do not need to save manually.
BrotherGym data is saved automatically as a JSON file `[JAR file location]/data/brothergym.json`. Advanced users are welcome to update data directly by editing that data file.

If your changes make the data file invalid, BrotherGym starts with an empty student list at the next run. The invalid file remains on disk until you run a command (BrotherGym saves after every command). Still, we recommend backing up the file before editing it.

Furthermore, certain edits can cause the BrotherGym to behave in unexpected ways (e.g., if a value entered is outside of the acceptable range). Therefore, edit the data file only if you are confident that you can update it correctly.
**Q**: How do I transfer my data to another computer?
**A**: Install the app on the other computer and overwrite the data file it creates with the data file from your previous BrotherGym home folder.

1. **When using multiple screens**, if you move the application to a secondary screen, and later switch to using only the primary screen, the GUI will open off-screen. The remedy is to delete the `preferences.json` file created by the application before running the application again.

2. **If you minimize the Help Window** and then run the `help` command (or use the `Help` menu, or the keyboard shortcut `F1`) again, the original Help Window will remain minimized, and no new Help Window will appear. The remedy is to manually restore the minimized Help Window.

**Add Student** | `addStudent NAME --hp PHONE_NUMBER --email EMAIL --addr ADDRESS [--tag TAG]... `
e.g., `addStudent James Ho --hp 22224444 --email jamesho@example.com --addr 123, Clementi Rd, 1234665 --tag friend --tag colleague`

**Edit Student** | `editStudent STUDENT_ID [--name NAME] [--hp PHONE_NUMBER] [--email EMAIL] [--addr ADDRESS] [--tag TAG]... [--clearTags]`
e.g.,`editStudent 2 --name James Lee --email jameslee@example.com`

**Add Workout Plan** | `addPlan PLAN_NAME --description DESCRIPTION --date DDMMYYYY [--tag TAG]... `
e.g., `addPlan Leg Day --description focus on form --date 20102026`

**Edit Workout Plan** | `editPlan PLAN_ID [--name PLAN_NAME] [--description DESCRIPTION] [--date DDMMYYYY] [--tag TAG]... [--clearTags]`
e.g.,`editPlan 2 --date 06072027`

**Add Exercise** | `addExercise EXERCISE_NAME --description DESCRIPTION`
e.g., `addExercise Squats --description 30kg * 3 sets * 5 reps`

**Edit Exercise** | `editExercise EXERCISE_ID [--name EXERCISE_NAME] [--description DESCRIPTION]`
e.g., `editExercise 1 --description 30kg * 3 sets * 10 reps`
